b:
Mingling with the wind,
entering the ear,
turning into love,
O music, who
could your creator be?

O spray of rain
that falls past the umbrella,
when I am soaked in your drizzle of music
my youth renews itself

O romance
that brings even the nine emotions
under your sway

You added richness
even to the pure Tamil
that lives in my thoughts

Wherever you went
you stood and showed
that you are a single language

O heart
of nature

Is it because
you are
the pulse
of God himself
that sound
became a scripture?

In the hearts of ordinary people
who know neither raga
nor rhythm
you spread and rise; and
to all the madmen
waiting for you to spread,
you become the great mystic

You are contained
in seven notes,
yet you make
countless souls long for you

O music,
part of everything
from my crying
to my laughter

I am a poor man
who must borrow
you
for the next hour
note: The "nine emotions" are the navarasas of Indian aesthetics; śṛṅgāra, romance, is traditionally the chief of them. The "seven notes" are the svaras of Indian music.
